_note: The Plot's seeds. Keyed by the same art families `brews.json` keys its ingredients by, so the eight seeds and the eight pairing ingredients are one set of eight buckets — which is what makes a harvest land somewhere the retort can use rather than opening a second economy beside it. A seed is not a component: no `PieceKind`, no `CATALOG` entry, no grid, and therefore no save seam.
_stages: Three per seed, and each contains the one before it. A crop that moved cells as it grew could be planted legally and then not fit, which is the stunting this game does not have — `Game::plant` refuses on the *harvest* shape for exactly that reason.

seeds.name: Kettle Scale Seed
seeds.blurb: A flake off something the works made, and it comes up as a thing with edges. Nobody planted the first one.

seeds.name: Toad Ichor Seed
seeds.blurb: It is not a seed and it is not a spawn. Put it in wet ground and in three fights there is something in the ground.

seeds.name: Cairn Dust Seed
seeds.blurb: Grey, dry, and it grows a grey dry thing that somebody at the works swears is a fern. It is not a fern.

seeds.name: Rust Bloom Seed
seeds.blurb: It wants iron in the ground and there is iron in every bed in this country. Cut it back twice and it comes up three times.

seeds.name: Tallow Drip Seed
seeds.blurb: Set in wax and planted in wax. It leans toward whatever is warmest, which in a Kettleworks bed is everything.

seeds.name: Silt Pearl Seed
seeds.blurb: Off the bottom of something that used to be a lake. It opens once, at the end, and closes for good an hour later.

seeds.name: Reef Salt Seed
seeds.blurb: Salt that came off a reef nobody has stood on. It will grow in a bed and it will take the bed with it.

seeds.name: Bone Meal Seed
seeds.blurb: Ground fine and sown thin. What comes up is white and comes up in rows whether or not it was sown in them.

_companions: Twenty-eight pairs, which is C(8,2) and complete — `every_pair_is_authored` counts it, because a table of twenty-eight written by hand is a table that can be twenty-seven. Two crops pay their pair when both are **ready** and their harvest shapes touch edge-on in the bed, which is `PerAdjacent`'s own question asked on a bed rather than on a board. Six of the twenty-eight pay an **ench seed** instead of a yield: that is the Plot's second door, and it opens onto enchs nothing else in the game sells.
